title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 7

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the warning-label session take place?
tasks.audioText: The electrical workshop tutor will review warning labels and equipment information on Tuesday at ten forty-five. Students should bring the safety-symbol reference sheet. The session will explain how warning text, symbols and equipment ratings help users recognise important information. Students will work with photographs and sample documents only.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which safety-symbol reference sheet is required for the warning-label lesson?
tasks.audioText: The electrical workshop tutor will review warning labels and equipment information on Tuesday at ten forty-five. Students should bring the safety-symbol reference sheet. The session will explain how warning text, symbols and equipment ratings help users recognise important information. Students will work with photographs and sample documents only.

tasks.prompt: An equipment label may show a voltage rating, current rating, model number and warning symbols. A technician records the information before preparing a report. If a label is damaged, the missing details should be confirmed using approved documentation. Guessing a rating can create confusion and may lead to an incorrect record, so unclear information should be reported for checking. Reading 1. Which details may appear on an equipment label?
options: Voltage and current ratings, model number and warning symbols
Supplier name, delivery date, purchase price and invoice number
Equipment colour, storage location, operator name and shift
Drawing revision, inspection date, batch quantity and room number

tasks.prompt: What should happen when a label is damaged?
options: Missing details should be estimated from a similar item
Missing details should be confirmed through approved documentation
The damaged label should be copied from another unit
The equipment should be used before the label is replaced

tasks.prompt: The equipment details ___ in the inspection record.
Choose TWO details that may appear on an electrical equipment label.
The stated electrical value that equipment is designed for is its rated ___.
A voltage rating is partly unreadable. What is the best response?
options: I will estimate the missing number.
The rating is unclear; could we confirm it from the approved documentation?
I will copy a rating from another model.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of electrical warning information in a logical order.
options: Confirm unclear details from approved documentation
correctOrder: Confirm unclear details from approved documentation

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining why electrical equipment labels should be read and recorded accurately. Include ratings, identification and warnings.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response explains why equipment labels should be read and recorded accurately (0–2); it addresses ratings, identification and warnings without guessing at unclear markings (0–2); the explanation is clear with understandable grammar (0–2); label/rating/electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
